intent.title: First execution wave: four reproduced Brief-Spec defects
intent.summary: User explicitly approved moving forward with the four reproduced defects and the shortest compliant execution route. The complete six-stage program remains in the task tracker; this is its first execution wave, not a reduction in overall scope.
success: Quoted or negated type/pivot examples cannot acquire explicit routing authority or break sticky classification; genuine overrides still take precedence.
Required typed outcomes and requested checkpoint modes cannot be skipped by clearing flags too early, and every repair path remains bounded.
Visible outcome or other report content mutations fail rendered verification even when embedded canonical JSON and hash remain unchanged; valid canonical renderings still pass.
Valid delivery references preserve private access, digest and expiry through normalization and snapshot derivation; repeated observations do not silently widen access or erase provenance.
out_of_scope: Remaining evolution capabilities stay in the full program and are not claimed complete by this wave.
No global installation, publication, push, merge or PR creation.
No edits outside the exact per-leaf source/test paths.
No model calls, scope authorization or hidden telemetry added to Brief-Spec core.

external_dependencies: Existing repository HMAC v3 key and explicit user authorization

evidence.summary: Four defects were independently reproduced during the preceding source inspection; the complete baseline suite subsequently passed. The repair scope and human authorization are recorded as distinct inputs.
